ScoreMethodology.heading: How we calculate your Match Score
ScoreMethodology.intro: Every programme gets a score from nine independent dimensions. Each is scored only when there's enough data — unknown never counts against you. The overall score is the weighted average of applicable dimensions.
ScoreMethodology.dim_academic: Your GPA, subject strengths and qualifications compared to the programme's published requirements.
ScoreMethodology.dim_budget: Tuition plus living costs versus the budget range you set in your profile, converted to one currency.
ScoreMethodology.dim_admission: Deadlines, entrance-exam requirements and how your profile lines up with what the programme asks for.
ScoreMethodology.dim_language: Whether the teaching language matches your preferences and meets certificate requirements (IELTS/TOEFL).
ScoreMethodology.dim_location: Country and city preferences, city size and university ownership type.
ScoreMethodology.dim_career: Overlap between your career priorities and the career tags attached to the programme.
ScoreMethodology.dim_format: Full-time vs part-time delivery against your stated preference.
ScoreMethodology.dim_lifestyle: City lifestyle tags (nightlife, nature, transport…) matched with what you said matters to you.
ScoreMethodology.dim_support: Objective facts: international office, Erasmus+ participation and guaranteed dormitory housing. Only scored when you opt in via profile.
ScoreMethodology.weightsBody: All dimensions start equally weighted. On Discover you can raise any single priority — that dimension then counts double in your scores everywhere.
ScoreMethodology.hardReqsBody: A few conditions are pass/fail rather than scored: degree level, English certificates and mathematics background where explicitly required. Failing a hard requirement flags the programme clearly instead of silently lowering its score.
ScoreMethodology.unknownHeading: Missing data is not a zero
ScoreMethodology.unknownBody: If a programme doesn't publish tuition or a dimension can't be evaluated, it's excluded from your average — never counted as a bad match. That's why two programmes with identical visible data can show different scores when one simply knows more about itself.
ScoreMethodology.confidenceBody: Every score carries a confidence level based on data freshness and completeness — high, medium or low. Treat low-confidence scores as starting points for research, not final answers.
ScoreMethodology.disclaimer: Scores are decision-support estimates built from public information, updated periodically. Always verify deadlines and requirements on the official university page before applying.

Privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
Privacy.intro: This policy explains what Unifind collects, why, and the control you have over it. Placeholder text — replace with counsel-reviewed copy before launch.
Privacy.s1Body: An email address and password for your account, plus the study preferences you enter in the questionnaire. Nothing else is required to use the matcher.
Privacy.s2Body: Solely to operate the service: authenticate you, calculate matches, save programmes you bookmark. We do not sell personal data or share it with universities without your explicit action (such as clicking an application link).
Privacy.s3Body: You can export or permanently delete your account and all associated data at any time from your Profile page — deletion cascades through every record immediately.
Privacy.s4Body: Only the session cookies required for sign-in. No advertising or third-party tracking cookies are set.

Terms.heading: Terms of Use
Terms.intro: By using Unifind you agree to these terms. Placeholder text — replace with counsel-reviewed copy before launch.
Terms.s1Body: Unifind aggregates publicly available information about universities and programmes to help you compare options. Scores are decision-support estimates, not admissions guarantees.
Terms.s2Body: Programme details change frequently. Always confirm deadlines, tuition and requirements on the official university website before applying or paying anything.
Terms.s3Body: Keep your credentials confidential. You are responsible for activity under your account and may delete it at any time from your Profile page.
Terms.s4Body: No scraping, automated bulk access, or attempts to disrupt the service. We may suspend accounts that abuse the platform.

Admin.importsDescription: Ingest programme/university data from a file: parse, validate, then insert with errors captured for review.
Admin.importsJsonHint: JSON: array of objects. Each object must have university_name, name, degree_level, field_name, language_code, duration_months, tuition_min, tuition_currency (tuition_max optional).
Admin.importsCsvHint: CSV: same columns in the header row, one programme per line.

Admin.settingsGrantHint: Paste a Supabase user UUID (anonymous sessions get one automatically). Access is immediate via RLS.
Admin.currencyDescription: EUR-based rates used for cross-currency budget comparisons. Synced from the European Central Bank's free daily feed.
Admin.currencyLastSynced: Last synced: {date, date, medium} {date, time, short}
Admin.currencyNote: EUR is fixed at 1 (the feed's base currency). Rates absent from the ECB feed keep their last value; the table is public-read/admin-write via RLS.
